lyrics:
[Intro: school bell, gang shout, bubbling synth riff, handclaps]
(Everybody out! Everybody out!)

[Verse 1: bass, claps and voice, riff answers each line]
The alarm goes off like a tiny lawyer
My daughter says, "Mom, you forgot how to play"
Kid, I wrote the manual on it
I just filed it under "someday"

[Chorus: full arrangement, gang shouts]
So call it recess (ring that bell!)
We've been good so long, been good so well
Put the grown-up down, let the wild one out
Call it recess
That's what it's all about
(Everybody out! Everybody out!)

[Verse 2: bass, claps and voice, hiccups and asides]
Three o'clock and the meeting's eternal
My mother texts, "Are you getting your rest?"
Ma, you didn't raise a spreadsheet
You raised a firework under a desk

[Chorus: full arrangement, gang shouts]
So call it recess (ring that bell!)
We've been good so long, been good so well
Put the grown-up down, let the wild one out
Call it recess
That's what it's all about
(Everybody out! Everybody out!)

[Synth Solo: wobbly whistling lead, chopped vocal snippets]

[Bridge: half-time, soft, sincere, close warm voice]
They take a kid who's all bright colors
Hand her beige and a set of keys
I'm gonna find that kid tonight
And tell her, "Come outside with me"

[Chorus: drum fill, bell, full arrangement]
So call it recess (ring that bell!)
We've been good so long, been good so well
Put the grown-up down, let the wild one out
Call it recess
That's what it's all about

[Final Chorus: squeals and spoken asides over the top]
Call it recess (ring that bell!)
We've been good so long, been good so well
Put the grown-up down, let the wild one out
Call it recess
That's what it's all about
(Everybody out! Everybody out!)

[Outro: call and response with the gang, last bell and a laugh]
(Everybody out!) Recess!
(Everybody out!) Call it recess!
(Everybody out!) Recess!
(Everybody out!)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 122 BPM, 4/4, G major, bouncing straight-eighth feel with a hint of reggae lilt in the guitar. Sunny, mischievous and impossible to sit still to.

VOICE: Bright female soprano with a quirky, characterful delivery: hiccups, squeaks, playful spoken asides and a slight street accent, sliding from a sweet coo to a full-throated belt. Gang backing vocals from a mixed crowd of women and kids on the 'everybody out' shouts.

INSTRUMENTS: A bubbling synth riff that sounds like a toy organ crossed with a marimba, playing a skipping, playground-chant melody (the earworm). Bouncy synth bass. Drum machine with crisp handclaps on every backbeat. Clean guitar playing light off-beat upstrokes. Bright synth-brass stabs in the chorus. A whistling, wobbly synth lead for the solo.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, a school bell rings, the gang shout, then the bubbling riff with claps for 8 bars. 0:16 Verse 1, bass, claps and voice with the riff answering each line. 0:32 Chorus 1, full arrangement with gang shouts. 0:56 Riff alone, 4 bars. 1:04 Verse 2. 1:20 Chorus 2. 1:44 Synth solo, the wobbly whistle lead playing a cheeky variation on the vocal tune. 2:08 Bridge, half-time feel, softer and suddenly sincere, voice close and warm. 2:32 Drum fill and bell, chorus 3. 2:56 Final chorus, with improvised squeals and spoken asides over the top. 3:20 Outro, call-and-response between the gang and the lead, riff bubbling on, ending with one last bell and a laugh at 3:55.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Bright, punchy and colourful. Claps and riff upfront, vocal dry and close so every hiccup is heard, a short bright reverb on the gang vocals.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The sincere half-time bridge, the one place the joke drops and she means it, followed by the bell that launches the last choruses.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Chopped, pitched snippets of the lead vocal dance around the synth solo. A real school bell is the song's recurring sound effect. Sub-bass keeps it club-ready.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Cheeky, liberated, briefly tender, then pure joy.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

The girl who came home at dawn in 1983 is now the grown-up with the alarm clock, the meeting and a daughter who says she has forgotten how to play. Tonight she rings the bell on herself.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a mums' night out anthem; a joyful burnout song for anyone chained to a desk; a daughter and mother singing to each other; a retirement party song; or a sequel to the original's spirit, in which the parent being talked back to is now the one singing. 'Put the grown-up down' works for every age over twenty-five.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: mini domestic scenes with a relative's voice in each verse, a playground-simple title, and a bridge that states the real stakes. The generational flip (the kid now tells the parent to have fun) is the modern point of view. Designed mishearing: 'Call it recess' is heard as 'Call it reckless', which improves it.
